root_cause.text: The nau8821 driver failed to cancel pending jack detection delayed work (`jdet_work`) during component removal, allowing the work function to execute after the driver module was unloaded, causing a use-after-free crash when accessing freed memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `nau8821_component_remove()` callback that calls `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&nau8821->jdet_work)` before driver removal. The crash trace shows `nau8821_jdet_work` being executed from the workqueue after module unload, attempting to call `snd_soc_dapm_disable_pin()` on freed kernel memory (address `ffffffffc10c2a20` in the unloaded module). The fix references commits that introduced the jdet_work mechanism, indicating the removal handler was never implemented to clean up this asynchronous work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add component removal handler to properly cancel jack detection delayed work and prevent resource leaks.
intent_record.what: Added a new static function `nau8821_component_remove()` that retrieves the driver data from the component, checks if jack detection is active, and cancels any pending delayed work if it is.
intent_record.how: This function provides cleanup logic that executes when the sound component is removed. It prevents resource leaks by ensuring the jack detection delayed work queue is properly cancelled before the component is torn down, avoiding potential use-after-free or orphaned work items.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the component remove callback to ensure proper cleanup and resource deallocation when the nau8821 audio component is removed.
intent_record.what: Added a new line `.remove = nau8821_component_remove,` to the `nau8821_component_driver` structure definition, assigning the `nau8821_component_remove` function as the remove callback handler.
intent_record.how: This change registers a cleanup/teardown function that will be invoked by the sound card framework when the component is being removed or unloaded. Previously, no remove handler was defined, meaning any necessary cleanup during component removal was not being performed.

candidates.rationale: The component driver structure is missing a .remove callback handler. Without registering a removal handler, the delayed work (jdet_work) is never cancelled when the component is removed, leading to use-after-free when the work function executes after module unload.

The probe function (nau8821_component_probe) returns without establishing any cleanup mechanism for the jack detection delayed work. There is no corresponding removal handler to cancel jdet_work, creating the vulnerability where pending work executes after driver unload.

vuln_statements.explanation: The component driver structure at line 1622 is missing a .remove callback handler. Without registering a removal handler in this structure, the delayed work (jdet_work) scheduled during probe is never cancelled when the component is removed, allowing it to execute after the driver module is unloaded, causing use-after-free.

The probe function (nau8821_component_probe) at line 1264 returns without establishing any cleanup mechanism for the jack detection delayed work (jdet_work). The absence of a corresponding removal handler means jdet_work is never cancelled, creating the vulnerability where pending work executes after driver unload and accesses freed memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in this initial driver commit. The `nau8821_jdet_work` delayed work is initialized in `nau8821_enable_jack_detect()` at line ~1570 with `INIT_WORK(&nau8821->jdet_work, nau8821_jdet_work)` and scheduled via `schedule_work(&nau8821->jdet_work)` in the interrupt handler at line ~1515. However, the `nau8821_i2c_remove()` function (lines ~1710-1715) only calls `devm_free_irq()` but does NOT cancel the pending `jdet_work`. This means if the work is scheduled but not yet executed when the module is removed, it will execute after the driver is unloaded, causing a use-after-free when accessing freed memory in `nau8821_jdet_work()`. The fix would require adding `cancel_work_sync(&nau8821->jdet_work)` in the remove function before or after freeing the IRQ.
